That's why I think which is so important that President Biden met with President Putin and relayed down the law, if you will. really made it very crystal clear that we don't like the direction that these cyber attacks are heading and we're drawing a line, we're making it clear that we are not going to tolerate this any further, that we will respond that either Russia is going to hold these bad actors accountable and really crack down on the cyber criminals operating within its borders or we're going to handle it. And what we don't want to see is escalate so that a more sensitive area of critical infrastructure is hit at a more sensitive time, say a natural gas pipeline in the debt of winter that could cause not only great damage to our economy, but could lead to loss of life. So we want to nip this in the bud now. I believe the Biden administration is on it. And we're going to do everything possible to make sure that we are more secure going forward. But this is a tough challenge. It is, by no means, we are out of the woods. And I would never say that we are ever going to be 100% cybersecurity. There's no such thing. There is no silver bullet. What we can do, though, is buy down our risk to something as much more manageable, closing that aperture of vulnerability to something as much more manageable than what it is today. And again, hold the bad actors accountable if they continue to hold us at risk.
